newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine GNP growth seen at 7 pct - ADB.
newsitem.headline: Philippine GNP growth seen at 7 pct - ADB.

text.p: The Philippines' gross national product (GNP) is expected to grow seven percent in 1997 and 1998 but further fiscal consolidation and a cautious monetary policy are needed, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Thursday.

"The economy now possesses the potential to grow at rates similar to those of its Southeast Asian neighbours, a feat that has eluded it ever since the balance of payments crisis of the early 1980s," the ADB said in its annual report.

"Realising this potential would require further efforts to upgrade the country's infrastructure and continued macroeconomic stability, involving further fiscal consolidation and a cautious monetary policy," it added.
GNP grew by 6.8 percent in 1996 after expanding five percent in 1995, while gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 5.5 percent against 4.8 percent in 1995.
The bank said the government's budget in recent years had been helped by a privatisation programme and lower interest payments.
But with lower receipts expected from privatisation this year and in the years ahead, there was a need for additional tax reforms and to reduce government expenditure, the report said.

The bank said the peso's appreciation in recent years may have led to the deterioration in the country's trade deficit, as the stronger local currency may have made the country's exports "Although it is unclear to what extent the appreciation of the peso contributed to this deterioration, further appreciation will put pressure on the trade balance, unless productivity in the tradeable goods sector keeps pace," it said.
In spite of interventions by the Philippine Central Bank, the peso had been strengthening in recent years due partly to remittances from overseas contract workers, it said.
The peso was at an average of 26.353 to the dollar on Wednesday, compared with 26.214 at the end of 1995.

The bank projects the country's trade deficit will widen to $15 billion in 1997 and $16 billion in 1998, while the current account deficit is seen increasing to $4.5 billion in 1997 and $5.0 billion in 1998.
The Philippines' trade deficit in 1996 was $11.79 billion, while the current account deficit was $3.56 billion.
